tool_input.description: Probe arch rule with violating files then remove them

result:
The newsletter sign-up is built as its own module under `modules/newsletter/`, and the blog code doesn't import anything from it. `bun run typecheck`, `bun test`, `bunx guren check` and `bunx guren check --arch` all pass with no failures, and so does the full `bunx guren gate`. The new tests cover subscribe, the 422 on an empty, invalid or already-subscribed address, confirm (including the 404 on an unknown token) and unsubscribe. To test the boundary rule, I temporarily added a file under `app/` importing the module's `index.ts` and one under `routes/` importing its schema. `check --arch` reported both as failures, and I then deleted them.

Things you might not expect:
- **`tsconfig.json` didn't cover `modules/`,** so the module's code wasn't being type-checked at all. I added `modules/**/*` to it.
- **`db/schema.ts` now has one line that re-exports the module's table.** The scaffolding command added it, and it's how the usual migrate command picks up the new table. The table itself is defined only in `modules/newsletter/db/schema.ts`.
- **Redirect "back" only follows a `Referer` from this site.** If it points at another site or is missing, the visitor goes to `/` instead, so the endpoint can't be used to bounce people to outside pages.
- **Addresses are trimmed and lowercased before saving,** the same way sign-up already handles them.

What I changed and where: I scaffolded the module with `bunx guren make:module newsletter`, which created `index.ts` (loaded under the `/newsletter` prefix) and registered it in `src/app.ts`. `modules/newsletter/db/schema.ts` defines the `newsletter_subscriptions` table with unique `email` and `token`, a nullable `confirmed_at`, and `created_at`, and `db/migrations/20260929162449_add_newsletter_subscriptions/` creates it. The data model is in `app/Models/NewsletterSubscription.ts` and the email check in `app/Http/Validators/NewsletterValidator.ts`, both under `modules/newsletter/`. `modules/newsletter/routes.ts` declares the three routes. Their handlers are in `modules/newsletter/app/Http/Controllers/NewsletterSubscriptionController.ts`: subscribe stores a 64-character random token, confirm sets `confirmed_at`, and unsubscribe deletes the row. The tests are in `modules/newsletter/tests/NewsletterSubscriptionController.test.ts`. A new `guren.arch.ts` at the project root adds the rule that fails the project's checks when anything in `app/` or `routes/` imports from `modules/newsletter/`, including type-only imports.
